subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get a first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The missing behavior is a public config and security boundary choice with upgrade and message-delivery consequences, so code can verify the gap but cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` or an equivalent cron-owned policy with documented precedence and focused migration/proof for existing cron jobs.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as subagent-like for tool policy, reducing new config surface but coupling cron behavior to subagent semantics.

options.title: Keep per-job controls only
options.body: Leave global cron defaults unimplemented and rely on `--tools`/`payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards for every scheduled job.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` or an equivalent cron-owned policy with documented precedence and focused migration/proof for existing cron jobs.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior routing and recent cron work make this the best available owner for the cron/security product-boundary decision.
